channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tokayev Orders Development of a 'People's Digital Economy'
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the creation of a 'people's digital economy'. The initiative aims to foster innovation and digital transformation across Kazakhstan, aligning with the nation's broader economic development goals. Further details on implementation are expected.

item.title: Tokayev Orders Further Decriminalization of Economic Offenses
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called for measures to further decriminalize economic offenses, citing ongoing appeals from entrepreneurs facing criminal prosecution. He emphasized the need for equal opportunities and fair competition, particularly for small and medium-sized businesses, and condemned actions that create artificial barriers for domestic producers.

item.title: Tajik Scientist Calls for Modernizing CIS Integration Model
item.description: A leading Tajik scientist has proposed updating the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) integration model. Shamsiddin Karimov suggested focusing on a socially oriented integration, emphasizing practical benefits for citizens such as education and cultural exchange, rather than solely relying on intergovernmental structures. He believes this approach is crucial for maintaining the CIS's relevance in the current geopolitical landscape.

item.title: Kazakh President Calls for Long-Term Financing System for Farmers
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the need for a long-term financing system to enable farmers to plan their work effectively. He urged the government to introduce efficient mechanisms for providing farmers with long-term investment resources, noting that while the agricultural sector grew significantly last year, current funds are often used for daily needs. The president also called for swift action on large-scale projects.

item.title: UN Chief: Women and Girls in Afghanistan Face Increasing Severe Restrictions
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that violations of women's and girls' rights in Afghanistan are escalating, with severe restrictions on their education and participation. He highlighted rising violence and discrimination, urging accountability for perpetrators and increased support for women-led organizations. The US deputy representative to the UN also condemned the Taliban's actions, noting a reversal of progress.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Begin Balkhash Nuclear Power Plant Construction Next Year
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed starting the construction of the "Balkhash" nuclear power plant next year and accelerating preparations for the "Moynkum" NPP. He emphasized the strategic importance of nuclear energy development for Kazakhstan and the need to ensure a continuous uranium supply for future power plants. Foreign companies are offering to establish high-tech production and train local specialists.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Stricter Control Over Water Consumption
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered stricter control over water consumption, emphasizing the need for rational water use and reducing losses in networks. He also called for the completion of a tariff reform in water consumption and the elimination of non-purposeful use of drinking water. The government is to finalize the National Information System for Water Resources.

item.title: Tokayev Criticizes Kazakhstan's Digitalization Approach, Calls for Digital Economy
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has criticized the country's approach to digitalization, stating that new technologies are often limited to automating existing processes rather than achieving real results. He made these remarks during his annual address to the nation, emphasizing Kazakhstan's obligation to create a digital economy.

item.title: Baiterek Holding Identifies Over 500 Billion Tenge Agro-Industry Projects
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev outlined agricultural development plans, noting a 6% growth last year and 15 trillion tenge in agro-industrial output. He stressed the need for long-term financing for farmers and instructed the government to implement effective methods for providing investment resources. Baiterek Holding has prepared a list of promising projects in the food industry exceeding 500 billion tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Needs to Fundamentally Change Geological Exploration Methods, Says President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that outdated methods are ineffective for discovering new mineral deposits. He emphasized the need to modernize geological exploration into a high-tech sector, utilizing advanced technologies for thorough subsurface research and ensuring data transparency. Attracting private investment into exploration and developing a national system for managing critical metal reserves were also highlighted.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Condemns Drinking Water Misuse at Car Washes
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called for an end to the non-purposeful use of drinking water, particularly at car washes, deeming it absurd. He instructed the government and regional administrations to tighten water consumption controls, reduce network losses, and implement a tariff reform for more responsible water management.

item.title: Kazakhstan Could Become Key Eurasian Food Hub in Global Famine Scenario, Says Tokayev
item.description: President Tokayev stated that Kazakhstan has the potential to be a primary food supplier for Eurasia in the event of a global famine. He emphasized the need to integrate artificial intelligence into agriculture, improve irrigation efficiency, and adopt water-saving technologies to boost crop yields and address water scarcity issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Investment Court in Alatau Based on English Common Law Model
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced plans to create an investment court in Alatau, modeled after English common law. This court will handle commercial disputes, aiming to enhance judicial quality and attract investment. Other legal matters will fall under the Civil Court's jurisdiction. Amendments to the constitutional law on Alatau's special legal regime are expected by January 2027.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Ban on Small Business Inspections from 2027 to 2029
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed a moratorium on inspections of small businesses. The proposed ban would be in effect from 2027 to 2029. This initiative aims to support the development of small and medium-sized enterprises within Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims for Energy Surplus by 2029, Prioritizing Renewables and Nuclear Power
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to achieve a stable energy surplus by 2029, requiring new power plants and modernized infrastructure, President Tokayev stated. The country will prioritize renewable energy sources like solar power and advanced coal technologies, while also planning for nuclear power plant construction. The long-term energy balance will be updated by 2035.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Special Legal Regime for Alatau City in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced that a special legal regime will be established in Alatau City. A corresponding bill, ensuring the operation of courts under an English model, will be submitted to the Kurultai by the end of January 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Heating Season Begins: Consumers Urged to Pay Gas Bills Promptly
item.description: As the cold weather and heating season approach, Gazprom Kyrgyzstan urges subscribers to check their balances and pay outstanding gas debts. Timely payments ensure uninterrupted gas supply and home comfort. Reconnection may take up to three working days after full debt settlement.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Discussing Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev suggested discussing the feasibility of a new three-year moratorium on inspections for micro and small businesses starting January 1, 2027. He noted that state control, while liberal, still impacts businesses through fines and unscheduled checks. Tokayev believes the moratorium experience from 2020-2023 was effective.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agro-Industrial Complex Output Reaches 15 Trillion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted the need for long-term financing for farmers. The agro-industrial complex output reached 15 trillion tenge last year, with a 6% growth. The "Baiterek" holding has identified promising food industry projects worth over 500 billion tenge, requiring immediate and accessible funding for modernization and quality project implementation.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Consolidating Investment Attraction Under "Baiterek" Holding
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed centralizing Kazakhstan's investment attraction efforts under the "Baiterek" holding to improve efficiency. He noted a lack of consistency in current investor relations, with various state bodies acting independently. The move aims to create a unified system for attracting and supporting investors in a competitive global market.

item.title: Kazakh President Highlights Critical Issues in the Energy Sector
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev identified significant challenges in Kazakhstan's energy sector, emphasizing its crucial role in economic sovereignty. He noted a shortage of professional energy specialists and a recurring annual deficit in electricity supply, forcing the country to purchase power at high prices from neighbors during winter and sell it back at reduced prices in summer.

item.title: Kazakh President Calls for Modern Approaches to Mineral Exploration
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the need for modern technologies in Kazakhstan's geological exploration. He stated that outdated methods are ineffective and urged a shift towards treating geology as a high-tech industry. Tokayev also highlighted the importance of studying the country's subsoil with advanced technologies and attracting private investment into exploration.

item.title: Kazakh President Questions Need for New Metallurgical Plants
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has expressed doubts regarding the necessity of constructing new metallurgical plants in Kazakhstan. The statement suggests a re-evaluation of industrial development strategies within the country's resource-rich economy.

item.title: Bishkek Lawmaker Demands Publication of Smog Investigation Findings
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Bishkek has requested the public release of investigation results concerning the city's smog problem. Citizens have complained about air pollution affecting Bishkek and surrounding areas. While five enterprises were found to be operating with environmental violations in 2024, the current situation and outcomes of subsequent checks remain unclear. The lawmaker urged for open publication of lab results and mitigation measures.

item.title: Border Clash in Angoor Adda; Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Calls Taliban Group Paranoid
item.description: A border clash occurred in Angoor Adda, with the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa labeling the Taliban group as paranoid. The governor stated that the Taliban group, which has been accused of entering Pakistani territory, has been warned. He emphasized that Pakistan's territory will not be allowed to be used for any purpose against Afghanistan. The governor also mentioned that the Taliban group has been warned not to enter Pakistani territory.

item.title: Iran Foreign Ministry Responds to Social Media Posts About Samarkand's Heritage
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Ismail Baqai, addressed controversy surrounding social media posts about Samarkand's historical heritage. He stated that some posts by embassies were intended as messages to the US. Baqai emphasized the importance of Iran-Uzbekistan relations and the shared heritage fostering friendly ties. Uzbekistan had previously summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest the posts, which have since been removed.

item.title: UK, UN, US Urge Greater Role for Afghan Women in Shaping Country's Future
item.description: The United Kingdom, the United States, and senior UN officials have called for Afghan women and girls to play a larger role in shaping their country's future. They criticized restrictions on women's rights and their exclusion from public life during a UN Security Council meeting on Women, Peace and Security.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Guarantee Fee for Cargo Transportation to Kazakhstan
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a guarantee fee for cargo transportation to Kazakhstan. A fee of 86,500 tenge (approximately 2.26 million soums) will be required for electronic queue registration at three border crossing points. The fee will be refunded if the driver arrives at the border on time.

item.title: Tajikistan Signs Agreements with EBRD for 62 Million Euros for Kulob Water Supply and Road Repair
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Finance and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) signed agreements totaling 62.085 million euros for two projects. One project, costing 9.9 million euros, will modernize the water supply and sanitation system in Kulob. The second project, valued at 52.185 million euros, will restore the Baljuvon-Sari-Khosor road.

item.title: Tajikistan and China Agree to Establish Environmental Laboratory
item.description: Tajikistan and China have agreed to establish an environmental laboratory at the National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan. The decision was made during a meeting between the academy's president and a representative from China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. The collaboration aims to enhance scientific and technical cooperation, including joint research projects and experience exchange.

item.title: Mecca Pact Officials Visit Tehran Amidst Regional Tensions
item.description: Senior officials from the 'Mecca Pact' countries, including Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, visited Tehran for high-level meetings. The visit is significant due to the potential for renewed conflict between Iran, the US, and Israel, and the perception of the pact as anti-Iranian. The pact's members are primarily Sunni and lean towards the West.

item.title: Study Reveals Significant Gender Gaps in Afghan School Textbooks
item.description: A study by the Georg Eckert Institute found deep gender gaps in textbooks published under the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan. The research examined Persian-language textbooks and educational policy documents. Findings indicate a discrepancy between government pledges for gender equality and the actual content of textbooks, which may be further impacted by Taliban plans.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explains Businessman's Travel After Release from Custody
item.description: Kazakhstan's Committee for Criminal Executive System clarified that businessman Kairat Boranbayev was not under probation control when he traveled to London. He was granted parole on June 1, 2026, and removed from probation supervision on June 18. Boranbayev, previously detained on embezzlement charges, had his sentence reduced and later replaced with a restriction of freedom.

item.title: Uzbekistan Advances Islamic Finance with New Opportunities
item.description: Uzbekistan is entering a new phase of Islamic finance development, creating opportunities beyond microfinance to include banks and the capital market. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov outlined a three-stage development plan and a roadmap for 2026–2030, including the introduction of new financial instruments. The changes aim to create new financial possibilities for the public and businesses.

item.title: Tajikistan-Kazakhstan Trade Surges 25.6% to $1.13 Billion in Nine Months
item.description: Trade turnover between Tajikistan and Kazakhstan increased by 25.6% in the first nine months of the year, reaching $1.13 billion. This represents a $230.9 million increase compared to the same period last year. Discussions at the 20th Intergovernmental Commission meeting in Dushanbe focused on removing trade barriers, simplifying customs procedures, and expanding cooperation in energy and food security.

item.title: Tajikistan Imposes Moratorium on Small and Medium Business Inspections Until 2029
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has signed a decree imposing a moratorium on all types of inspections for small and medium-sized businesses until January 1, 2029. The decree, excluding tax authority inspections, aims to support entrepreneurship, strengthen industrial and export potential, and create favorable conditions for business development and investment. Previous moratoria have positively impacted business growth and job creation.

item.title: US Official Condemns Taliban's Restrictions on Women and Girls in Afghanistan
item.description: US Deputy Representative to the UN, Tammy Bruce, condemned the Taliban's restrictions on women and girls, calling for their immediate end. She stated that the Taliban had erased decades of progress in peace and security and deemed restrictions on education and employment unacceptable. The US remains committed to defending women's rights and promoting their economic empowerment.

item.title: Reports: Men in Russia allegedly abducted and forced to sign military contracts
item.description: Residents in Omsk, Russia, are reporting that men are being abducted from the streets and forced to sign contracts with the Ministry of Defense. Activists cite user reviews on 2GIS, with one user claiming her father-in-law was beaten after being taken to a recruitment center. Another report states a man who came to Omsk for work disappeared and later signed a contract.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches Apple Pay; local Uzcard and Humo support coming soon
item.description: Apple Pay officially launched in Uzbekistan on October 27, allowing users to link Visa and Mastercard cards from several banks. The Central Bank announced that support for local Uzcard and Humo payment systems will be introduced soon. This expansion will allow users to make payments using their Apple devices.

item.title: Taliban Border Attack in Pakistan Kills One Civilian, Injures Five
item.description: Taliban forces reportedly opened fire on residential areas near the Angoor Ada border crossing in South Waziristan, Pakistan. The attack resulted in the death of one civilian and injuries to five members of a family. Pakistan's army responded with decisive action, reportedly destroying several Taliban outposts.
